title: CLEAR: Addressing Representation Contamination in Multimodal Healthcare Analytics

problem.claim: Multimodal EHR analytics requires extracting modality-specific information and modeling modality correlations for clinical decision-making.

gap.claim: Existing methods generally overlook contaminated representations in routine EHR data, allowing less relevant representations and false-positive correlations to impair recognition of effective representations.

contributions.claim: CLEAR is a counterfactual disparity learning model for explicit multimodal EHR analytics that models representation contamination and calibrates and enhances representations.

CLEAR uses counterfactual prompt learning to capture representation discrepancy, adaptive dynamic imputation to decouple elementwise representations, and gating to incorporate discriminative discrepancy information.
CLEAR establishes intra- and inter-modality correlations through a multimodal representation fusion module for downstream analytic tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that CLEAR is the first model to model and resolve representation contamination in multimodal EHR analytics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two real-world datasets reportedly show that CLEAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines for multimodal healthcare analytics.

narrative_sequence.summary: EHRs are presented as the standard data source for comprehensive patient-condition analysis.
Existing methods extract modality-specific information and model modality correlations for clinical decision-making.
These methods generally overlook contaminated representations that can weaken discriminative ability.
CLEAR models representation contamination, calibrates and enhances representations, and fuses multimodal correlations for downstream tasks.
The authors report consistent outperformance of state-of-the-art baselines on two real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Less relevant representations associated with false-positive correlations may impede recognition of truly effective representations.

interpretation.claim: Multimodal models may benefit from explicitly identifying and calibrating representation-level contamination before fusion.

application.claim: For multimodal healthcare analytics, inspect representation discrepancy and use calibration or selective enhancement before downstream fusion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported multimodal EHR setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe implementation details, ablations, limitations, or computational costs.
